A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RS-CL research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoboCasa-Kitchen and LIBERO experiments, real-robot evaluations, representation analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds TCN comparisons, representation probes, robustness studies and evaluations on additional robot embodiments.

M1.justification: v3 adds an autoregressive instantiation of RS-CL on π0-FAST, which predicts action tokens through next-token prediction instead of flow matching (Appendix E.3). The RS-CL formula, state-distance weighting, summarization token and view-cutoff mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds DexMimicGen evaluations involving bimanual Panda arms with Inspire Hands and a GR-1 humanoid, substantially broadening embodiment and state-space coverage (Appendix E.4). It also adds real-robot testing under darker lighting. RoboCasa-Kitchen, LIBERO and the previous real-robot scenarios remain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds reported comparisons with DreamGen, DUST, Video Policy, FLARE and HAMLET. Table 3 additionally evaluates single-view and multi-view TCN. Conversely, the plain InfoNCE comparator in v1's LIBERO Table 6 disappears, although the RoboCasa 300-demonstration InfoNCE ablation remains.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures include DTW-aligned, 32-class task-phase prediction using KNN with k=5; TCN comparisons with a 0.2-second temporal margin; compute profiling; and sweeps over schedules, temperatures, projection dimensions and batch sizes. The previously stated RoboCasa/LIBERO training budgets and evaluation trial counts are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds hyperparameter sensitivity studies, scene/task-phase representation probes, lighting robustness tests, architecture and state-configuration checks, and task-group analysis. These examine robustness, mechanisms and applicability beyond v1's analyses. The expanded plain-InfoNCE analysis in v1 Appendix D.1 is removed, while the original main design ablations and CKNNA analysis remain.

E5.justification: v3 Table 8 reports separate results for training seeds 0, 7 and 42, and Figures 4 and 6 introduce error bars on average success rates. v1 supplies neither. The error-bar definition is unspecified, and the new seed reporting does not establish how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: The principal RoboCasa and LIBERO results remain 69.7% and 96.4%. New results include TCN success rates of 50.0/50.3% versus RS-CL's 53.0%, π0-FAST+RS-CL results, and DexMimicGen baseline/RS-CL results of 52.7/57.3% and 68.9/73.1%. Additional low-data SigLIP2 and plain-InfoNCE results are omitted. New Table 12 introduces inconsistent pick-and-place baseline averages: 30.1/55.6%, versus 30.8/55.3% in Figure 4 and the retained task-level results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical content, with equivalent notation and additional explanation. Neither version provides formal propositions or proofs, and v3 introduces no substantive theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain state-aware contrastive regularization, lightweight view-cutoff augmentation, and improved simulation and real-robot performance. v3's abstract highlights the overall 69.7% RoboCasa result already reported in v1; the additional experiments support the existing contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning preservation of scene information alongside task-progress alignment, stronger benefits for less constrained tasks, and applicability across action-modeling paradigms and state configurations. It also explains TCN's computational overhead. The earlier LIBERO batch-size explanation disappears, while the object-pose/contact-force limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents per-dimension state normalization, two A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs and 64 CPU cores, training times, and implementation details for TCN and KNN analyses. Existing checkpoint, dataset and main training instructions remain; v1's pseudocode is removed. These disclosures do not establish changed settings for the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DreamGen, DUST, HAMLET, Video Policy, DexMimicGen and DROID, while dropping the original RoboBrain and Open X-Embodiment references. It sharpens the distinction from separate contrastive pretraining, but retains the same broad related-work organization and research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative remain, with language polishing and localized rewrites. Simulation and real-robot setup descriptions are separated, and appendix material is regrouped. The reproducibility and LLM-use statements are removed, while an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. The original RoboCasa comparison is redistributed into an expanded leaderboard and demonstration-count chart. Real-robot figures are redesigned, the standalone close-lid comparison disappears, and new analysis tables, lighting examples and an annotated representation visualization substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central efficiency and applicability claims through TCN comparisons, measured computational costs, quantitative representation probes, seed checks, and autoregressive and complex-embodiment tests. These address important validation gaps in v1. The gains outweigh lost auxiliary results and reporting defects, including undefined error bars, inconsistent Table 12 averages, and the claimed 1.25% training-time overhead when Table 6 implies approximately 1.86%.
